canvas-01-1.description: The northern end of the North Main Street strip on Sheet 1 of the April 1928 Barnegat atlas, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. North Main Street runs straight up the left half of the part with frontages on both sides, house numbers running from about 348 to 367 on the east side and 390 to 409 on the west. Cedar Street leaves North Main Street eastward near the middle of the part as a 30 ft street; its lots 15 to 27 are drawn up to the heavy line that separates the part from the sheet's key map and index. The blocks are numbered 14 and 15 above Cedar Street and 4 below it, and are given over to scattered frame dwellings with stables, sheds and garages set well back in large lots; an auto repair shop of concrete block stands near the top on the west side, a vacant and dilapidated garage with an earth floor on the east side further south. A six-inch water pipe runs along North Main Street and the hydrants are marked. Much of the east side is left as open land marked vacant beyond, and the area east of the heavy dividing line is marked no exposure. The sheet's compass rose sits on the part's south-east edge and the scale bar in its lower left corner. This strip continues south in part 2 of the same sheet, which reaches Burr Street; the two strips overlap by roughly 130 ft on the ground.
notes: North Main and Cedar are North Main Street and Cedar Street today.

Placed from the one junction drawn (Cedar / North Main) with the atlas scale and the rotation of the measured lines; Water Street and Rosehill Road, which meet North Main Street here today, are not drawn.

Printed Sheet 1 (canvas labelled Index): title, key, water/fire notes, 1000 ft key map, index and location map in the upper right, with a 50 ft map in two columns: part 1 North Main Street north of Cedar Street (left), part 2 North Main Street north of Burr Street (lower right). Each has one junction; anchored.

canvas-01-2.description: The southern half of the North Main Street strip on Sheet 1, drawn as a separate column to the right of part 1 at 50 feet to an inch, from Burr Street at the bottom edge northward for about 660 ft. North Main Street runs up the right-hand side of the part with house numbers 370 to 379 on the east and 380 to 388 on the west, an eight-inch water pipe beneath it. Block 15 on the west side is divided into deep lots with frame dwellings, coops, sheds and a storage building; block 4 on the east side has a few dwellings near the street and is otherwise vacant. At the top of the east side is the Barnegat Water Company's plant: a concrete-block pumping station with an automatic centrifugal electric pump and a gasoline engine, a Deming power pump, and a steel standpipe or water tower of 50,000 gallons. In the lower left corner the Central Railroad of New Jersey is lettered along the edge of the part where it meets Burr Street. Burr Street is drawn only along the bottom edge; its continuation south of it is on Sheet 3. Heavy lines separate the part from part 1 to the west and from the index above.
notes: North Main is North Main Street today; Burr St. is Burr Street.
Placed from one hand-picked point (Burr / North Main) at the atlas scale with north taken from the bearing of modern North Main Street (about 22 degrees); low confidence.

Printed Sheet 1 (canvas labelled Index): title, key, water/fire notes, 1000 ft key map, index and location map in the upper right, with a 50 ft map in two columns: part 1 North Main Street north of Cedar Street (left), part 2 North Main Street north of Burr Street (lower right). Each has one junction; anchored.

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of Sheet 2, drawn at 50 feet to an inch: the west side of Barnegat along West Bay Avenue from the railroad westward for about 1,000 ft, with Burr Street in the north-east corner. West Bay Avenue crosses the part from side to side with house numbers 101 to 111 and 201 to 203 on the north and 112 to 124 and 222 to 224 on the south. At the right edge the Tuckerton Railroad runs down the sheet with North Railroad Avenue and South Railroad Avenue beside it and a freight house with platform north of West Bay Avenue. Burr Street runs west from the railroad with lots 101 to 114; north and south of it the land is in large deep lots, mostly vacant. The blocks are numbered 16, 17 and 7. South of West Bay Avenue are dwellings, an R.C. chapel and a cement block manufactory drawn from plans; north of it are dwellings and the Hotel Barnegat at the corner of North Railroad Avenue, and west of them an unnamed cemetery. Four- and six-inch water pipes run along West Bay Avenue. Heavy lines cut out two other parts of the sheet: West Bay Avenue further west in the upper left corner (not placed) and East Bay Avenue east of Sheet 4 in the lower left corner (part 3).
notes: W. Bay is West Bay Avenue today; North Railroad Av. corresponds to Memorial Drive, which follows the former railroad.

Placed from two points along West Bay Avenue (its junction with Memorial Drive and a point on modern West Bay Avenue 979 ft west of it); modern parcel lines through this placement match the drawn lots closely. Low to medium confidence.

50 ft. Three parts: 1 main (West Bay Av west of the railroad, Burr St, N./S. Railroad Av, cemetery, Hotel Barnegat); 2 upper-left box: West Bay further west, lots 15-37, no cross street (not placed); 3 lower-left box: East Bay continuing east from sheet 4 (placed from a point carried from sheet 4 and a point on modern East Bay Av).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: upper-left box: West Bay Avenue further west (lots 15-37, blocks 17 and 7) (no street junction or stated distance; only the line of West Bay Avenue is known; needs position along West Bay Avenue, e.g. parcel corners (locate.py corner) matched to the drawn lots).

sheet-2-3.description: A strip of East Bay Avenue in the lower left corner of Sheet 2, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and separated from the rest of the sheet by a heavy line. It continues East Bay Avenue eastward from the right-hand edge of Sheet 4 (the number 4 at its west end points there): the road enters from the west sloping down the sheet, bends and runs straight east to the edge of the part. House numbers run from 301 to 312 on the north side and 313 to 321 on the south side, and a four-inch water pipe runs under the street. Block 18 north of the road is mostly marked vacant beyond, with a vacant and dilapidated dwelling; block 19 to the south has a row of frame dwellings in narrow lots. The sheet's scale bar and copyright line are printed in the part's lower left corner, and a north arrow stands in block 19.
notes: E. Bay is East Bay Avenue today.

Placed from two points: East Bay Avenue's centre at the join with Sheet 4 (carried from Sheet 4's placement) and a point on modern East Bay Avenue 621 ft further east. The drawn bend in the road is gentler than today's, so the fit rotates the part about 19 degrees from Sheet 4; low confidence.

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of Sheet 3, drawn at 50 feet to an inch: the centre of Barnegat around the crossing of Main Street and Bay Avenue, from Burr Street at the top to an alley at the bottom and from the railroads on the west to Maple Avenue on the east. North Main Street and South Main Street run down the middle; West Bay and East Bay cross them at the junction near the post office. Birdsall Street runs north from East Bay on the right. Along the west side the Tuckerton Railroad and the Central Railroad of New Jersey run parallel with North and South Railroad Avenue between them, with two passenger depots, a lumber shed and a bank near West Bay. The commercial blocks hold stores, the Barnegat Opera House, the Almont Inn, a Masonic (F. and A.M.) lodge, the Barnegat Fire Company's fire department, the post office, a printing shop, a tin shop and the W. G. Conrad lumber yard with its lumber piles and building supply store. Institutions include the Methodist Episcopal church and the Barnegat Public School at the top right. House numbers run 98 to 140 on Main Street and 401 to 436 on Bay. Water pipes of four to eight inches are drawn along the main streets. A heavy line cuts out an inset of Birdsall Street in the lower left corner (part 2).
notes: N. Main and S. Main are North Main Street and South Main Street; W. Bay and E. Bay are West Bay Avenue and East Bay Avenue; Centre St. is Center Street; North Railroad Av. corresponds to Memorial Drive.

Only five street junctions are detectable, four of them along Bay Avenue, so the leave-one-out error (10 m) is large although the fit residuals are about 1.3 m; modern parcel lines through the placement match the drawn lots well.

50 ft. Town centre: N./S. Main, W./E. Bay, Birdsall, Maple Av, Burr St, Railroad Avs, two railroads. Part 2 is an inset (lower left) of Birdsall north of the main map's top edge, placed from a carried point.

sheet-3-2.description: An inset in the lower left corner of Sheet 3, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and at the same angle as the main part, showing Birdsall Street north of the top edge of the main map. Birdsall Street, 35 ft wide, runs up the inset; lots 7 and 8 lie on its west side and lots 9 to 14 on its east side, the numbering continuing with lot 15 at the top of the main part, and the number 3 at the bottom points back to the main map. Block 1 on the east side holds a few frame dwellings and outbuildings; block 4 on the west is empty. The top of the inset is marked vacant beyond. A north arrow is drawn in the upper left corner. The inset is bounded on the east by the heavy line that also marks the edge of South Railroad Avenue in the main part.
notes: Birdsall is Birdsall Street today.
Placed from one point carried from the main part's top edge (where the lot numbering continues) with the main part's scale and rotation; no junction is drawn. Low confidence.

50 ft. Town centre: N./S. Main, W./E. Bay, Birdsall, Maple Av, Burr St, Railroad Avs, two railroads. Part 2 is an inset (lower left) of Birdsall north of the main map's top edge, placed from a carried point.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4, drawn at 50 feet to an inch: the residential blocks east of the centre, between Maple Avenue on the west and School Street on the east, from above East Bay to East Brooks at the bottom. East Bay crosses the upper part of the sheet sloping down to the east, with house numbers 220 to 268 and 238 to 252; Centre runs parallel to it below, and East Brooks along the bottom with numbers 201 to 233. Ridgeway leaves East Bay northward near the right, and North School Street and South School meet East Bay a little further east; a 30 ft street joins Ridgeway and North School Street at the top. Blocks 1, 2, 18, 19, 20 and 25 are divided into narrow lots with frame dwellings, many with stables and sheds. Near the corner of South School and East Brooks are boat building works with machine and woodworking shops, and storage buildings for boats and lumber. Four- and six-inch water pipes run under East Bay, Maple Avenue, School and East Brooks. The area south of East Brooks is drawn as lots marked vacant beyond. The number 2 at the east end of East Bay points to the strip on Sheet 2 that continues it.
notes: E. Bay is East Bay Avenue; Centre is Center Street; E. Brooks is Brook Street; N. School St. is Walnut Lane together with the 30 ft street at its north end; S. School is Iowa Street north of Center Street and School Street south of it; Ridgeway is Ridgeway Street.
The junction of East Bay Avenue and Walnut Lane was rejected (17 m): the modern node does not sit where North School Street meets East Bay on the sheet.
50 ft. One part: E. Bay, Centre, E. Brooks, Maple Av, Ridgeway, N. School St (= Walnut Lane), S. School (= Iowa St / School St).

sheet-5-1.description: The main part of Sheet 5, drawn at 50 feet to an inch: the south end of the village along South Main Street from West and East Brooks at the top to below Bennett Neck Road. South Main Street runs down the middle with house numbers 201 to 239; West Brooks and East Brooks meet it slightly offset, and East Brooks runs up to Maple Avenue at the top right corner. South Railroad Avenue and the Tuckerton Railroad run down the left side, with A. P. Claxton's feed, grain, wood and coal business and its siding by West Brooks. Below West Brooks lies the Newbury Lumber Company's yard with lumber sheds, lumber and cement storage and a foundation. A brook crosses the sheet from the railroad to the right edge. North of the brook are the Presbyterian church, a garage for 15 cars and dwellings; further south a lane runs west from South Main Street, and a second garage for 20 cars stands by Bennett Neck Road. A building with an engine room stands west of the railroad below Bennett Neck Road. Heavy lines cut out three other parts of the sheet: Ridgeway in the upper left corner (part 2), South Main Street further south in the lower left (part 3, not placed) and the Barnegat Glass Company on North Main Street in the lower right (part 4, not placed).
notes: W. Brooks and E. Brooks are Brook Street; S. Main is South Main Street; Bennett Neck Rd. is Hillside Avenue; South Railroad Av. corresponds to Memorial Drive along the former Tuckerton Railroad.
West and East Brooks meet South Main Street offset by about 30 ft; the junction was hand-picked at the centre of the two.
The seam pass proposed an 8 to 11 m move against Sheet 4 from a single low-score match; it was not applied (seam_correction false).

sheet-5-2.description: An inset in the upper left corner of Sheet 5, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, showing Ridgeway further north than Sheet 4 reaches. A note at its lower edge reads 585 ft to Bay St., measured down Ridgeway to East Bay. Ridgeway, 28 ft wide, runs up the inset with house numbers 101 to 106 on the west side and 107 to 112 on the east, and a six-inch water pipe; a hydrant is marked near the bottom. Block 18 on the east side has a few frame dwellings, one with a note of a two-storey frame barn 135 ft away; block 1 on the west side holds a dwelling and a storage building, and the land beyond is marked vacant. Heavy lines separate the inset from the main part of the sheet to the east and from the South Main Street inset below.
notes: Ridgeway is Ridgeway Street today.
